rows.name: VIX level and risk regime
rows.registered_verdict: Exact-session direction and incremental value are unmeasured; conditional regime candidates only.
rows.effect: the level abstains at or above 30 and never votes on direction
rows.assumption: Three rows read VIX and none may vote, so a single market signal cannot be outvoted by duplicated volatility evidence.

rows.name: VIX level and change at the cutoff
rows.registered_verdict: Matched spot VIX duplicates F1; consolidate ownership and remove any independent duplicate vote.
rows.effect: consolidated onto the same VIX level as live.f1; no second reading and no second vote
rows.assumption: The row is treated as a duplicate of the regime gate rather than as an independent signal.

rows.name: US 2Y yield, five-session change
rows.declared_role: decomposition only, DGS2 is counted inside F19
rows.registered_verdict: A plausible policy channel does not establish next-session direction; no fixed sign or weight survives.
rows.effect: the five-interval DGS2 change must be present and fresh, but it is excluded from every family
rows.assumption: The row says DGS2 is counted inside F19. Requiring the raw change as well makes the evidence gate stricter than the vote set without changing a call.

rows.name: US minus Germany 2Y spread, five-session change
rows.registered_verdict: Relative-policy mechanism survives; the exact-session predictive contribution has no measurement.
rows.effect: one vote from the US minus Germany 2Y spread at a 5 bp threshold

discrepancies.finding: The DGS2 five-interval change is required by the evidence gate and excluded from every family. A morning can be blocked by an input that cannot change the call.
discrepancies.consequence: Coverage is stricter than the vote set: eight of the nine inputs can block and only six can vote.
discrepancies.proposed_change: v0.1.1: state the requirement as an operand of the spread rather than a ninth standalone gate.

discrepancies.finding: The row names VIX level and change at the cutoff. The executable reads the level only; no VIX change is among the nine inputs.
discrepancies.consequence: The regime gate cannot react to a VIX move, only to its level.
discrepancies.proposed_change: v0.1.1: add a VIX one-day change to the gate, or retitle the row as level-only.

discrepancies.finding: inputs.json gives the ICE row a maximum age of zero hours, and engine.js also requires observed <= published <= received <= cutoff. Together those force observed = published = received = the cutoff instant, so a live morning can only pass with a zero-latency receipt stamped at 05:00:00.000. The supplied fixture passes because it stamps all three clocks at the cutoff.
discrepancies.consequence: Sealed live proof for the ICE vote is impossible under v0.1.0 as written, and every historical morning stays blocked even if licensed fixings are acquired.
discrepancies.proposed_change: v0.1.1: let the ICE row read the previous eligible 05:00 fixing with a maximum age of 24 hours, and require the receipt by the cutoff rather than at it.

discrepancies.finding: Two calendar rows share one input. The event gate counts releases in [cutoff, endpoint); distance since or until an event has no executable representation.
discrepancies.consequence: The count is the only calendar feature, so 'shared F23' is a declaration rather than an implemented rule.
discrepancies.proposed_change: v0.1.1: either implement distance as a separate context field or record F23 as unimplemented in the rulebook table.

discrepancies.finding: The integrity gate has no fallback by design, so an input that is missing, stale, unclocked or substituted blocks the whole morning.
discrepancies.consequence: One absent series blocks a morning even when the remaining votes are complete.

discrepancies.finding: The trace carries votes.front even though frontCounted is false and no family reads it. A reader adding the trace's votes would double count the US leg.
discrepancies.consequence: The fixture trace is complete, but the front vote must be read as reported-only.
discrepancies.proposed_change: v0.1.1: rename the trace field to frontReportedOnly and publish the counted vote set beside it.

discrepancies.finding: The 0.30 per cent broad-dollar, 0.15 per cent ICE and 1 per cent gold and QQQ thresholds are proposed noise filters with no measured sign.
discrepancies.consequence: The bands are hypotheses; they are not calibrated and carry no probability.

discrepancies.finding: Eleven rows read five inputs. Eight rows across spread, real yield, broad dollar, ICE, gold and QQQ produce six votes; two rows each on spread and real yield produce one vote each.
discrepancies.consequence: The 25-row book yields six votes in three equal-weight families, not 25 signals.

discrepancies.finding: The candidate's trace lists all 25 rows, and the ten rows with no feed carry a null value. The trace therefore shows 25 entries over nine measurements.
discrepancies.consequence: A complete factor trace means every row is present and labelled, not that every row was measured.

discrepancies.finding: The event gate is only as good as the archived schedule. The staged calendar carries FOMC statements and none of the four other required release families.
discrepancies.consequence: A zero count cannot be read as 'no release occurred' until the omitted schedules are archived.

instrument.label: DXY.cash (FTMO spot CFD)
instrument.clock_rule: the terminal stamps bars in server time; the exporter converts to UTC with the US daylight-saving dates (UTC+2 outside, UTC+3 inside) and reproduces that shift against the UTC EUR/USD tape before writing
instrument.what_it_is_not: not the ICE cash index (no official settlement print, broker hours, broker spread) and not FRED DTWEXBGS

source_amendments.eligibility: The current observation is the close of the one-hour bar that ends at the 05:00 London cutoff, so the value is complete at the decision instant and no lookahead is possible. The previous observation is the same construct on the most recent preceding London date inside a four-calendar-day cap, which covers the weekend and a single holiday. Elapsed hours are recorded on every record; a wider gap is refused, not bridged.
differences: Source identity: a broker spot CFD quote stream (FTMO Global Markets Ltd, symbol DXY.cash) instead of the official ICE US Dollar Index spot print. Only the declared fields change; the arithmetic does not.
Sampling: the observation is the close of a completed one-hour bar, not a single official fixing print. The bar's last tick is the 05:00:00 London price.

Bar convention: this input reads the bar that ENDS at the cutoff (04:00-05:00 London). Test 1's DXY lane reads the bar that OPENS at the cutoff (05:00-06:00 London) at both endpoints, because an outcome may be measured after the fact. The two lanes are therefore shifted by one hour and must never be quoted as one series.

Previous-eligible interval: 24 hours on a normal weekday, 72 hours across a weekend, up to 96 hours across a holiday. The elapsed interval is published per record, so a three-day return is never presented as a one-day return.

Missing bars: the tape carries no bar on a weekend or holiday 05:00 boundary and none in the broker's closed hours. Such a morning is blocked and absent from the evidence file; no neighbouring hour is borrowed and nothing is interpolated.

Clock: the record's observed and published clocks are the bar-completion instant, which equals the cutoff by construction. The export is retrospective, so this is a completion clock, not a recipient receipt: `received_at_utc` stays null and sealed live replay remains blocked for this input.
Quote quality: broker spreads, broker hours and three-decimal quoting replace an official settlement print. Levels are not comparable across the two instruments; only the simple return is used.
limitations: A morning without its own 05:00 bar is blocked, so the input cannot reach every session in the run window.
No receipt exists for any historical morning, so the ice input can reach the historical reconstruction lane only.
The amendment does not touch test 1: the official lane stays blocked and labelled, and the broker lane stays the labelled control it already was.

equivalence.verdict: Equivalent on clean weeks, different across holidays. Where the five-interval window spans no Treasury non-publication day the two agree on 540 of 541 mornings, which proves the transform, units and alignment. Where the window spans a holiday they agree on 12 of 120, and the gap is a missing-observation policy: the legacy scalar filled the holiday, this reconstruction uses the five most recent published observations and refuses to fill. The instrument and the publisher are the same either way.
equivalence.disproof_hook: Re-run `npm run check:h1-a02`: if the clean-week share falls below 99 or any recorded figure drifts, the transform, the units or the alignment is wrong and the amendment must be withdrawn. The check reads only committed artefacts (`data/usd-layer1-backtester/run-v1.json`, `data/usd-layer1-backtester/h1-v1/real.json`), so it reproduces on a clean checkout.

differences: Publisher of record: the series is read from the U.S. Department of the Treasury instead of being attributed to the H.15 release, which does not carry real yields.
Instrument: unchanged. DFII10 is the Treasury's 10-year constant-maturity real yield whether FRED, H.15 or the Treasury CSV is quoted.
Transform: unchanged - five completed observation intervals, reported in basis points.
Clock: the publication instant is reconstructed from the publisher's stated release time and recorded per record with its margin to the cutoff. No receipt is claimed.
limitations: The reconstruction assumes the stated release time was met on every historical day. A late print is not excluded by this evidence; late-print rejection remains an untested gate.
No receipt exists for any historical morning, so this input can reach the historical reconstruction lane only.
The amendment changes what the audit evaluates. The supplied package stays frozen and byte for byte as delivered.

The legacy scalar matches the Treasury recomputation on clean weeks and diverges on windows that span a Treasury non-publication day, so the two are not the same series on holiday weeks (see `equivalence`).

candidates.title: Measure H.10 freshness on the publication clock, not the observation date
candidates.supplied_outcome: 564 of 725 mornings fresh; 161 blocked although the newest release at the cutoff was hours old
candidates.proposed_rule: fresh = cutoff - published_at_utc <= the same 192h window AND release_is_latest_at_cutoff = true. The window is unchanged; only the quantity it measures changes, from the observation date to the release time of the newest publication.
candidates.rationale: H.10 is a weekly release. Its Friday value is first published on the following Monday at 16:15 ET, so an observation-age rule charges the model for the publisher's cadence rather than for the age of the information it holds. The latest-release condition keeps the rule strict: a record whose release was already superseded at the cutoff stays blocked.
evidence: The Federal Reserve publishes H.10 on Monday at 16:15 ET, covering the previous business week.
Every broad record is rebuilt offline from the dated weekly release pages, so published_at_utc is the release page date and the vintage is a first publication.
No publication age exceeds the supplied window; the observation ages do, on Mondays and on the Tuesdays that follow a market holiday.
candidates.disproof: Find one session where the newest H.10 release published at or before the cutoff is not the record's release, or where a release page shows a value that was first published earlier than the dated page carrying it. Either finding voids the candidate for that session.
candidates.does_not_license: It does not shorten the window, accept a bounded or reconstructed release time, or carry over to another input: each input needs its own cadence argument.

candidates.title: Treat an event schedule as applicable knowledge, not as a decaying observation
candidates.supplied_rule: fresh = cutoff - observed_at_utc <= 24h, with the required release types present
candidates.supplied_outcome: no imported calendar bundle exists, so the supplied freshness rule and the applicability rule both block every morning; the size of the proposal cannot be measured until a schedule is imported
candidates.proposed_rule: A schedule record is applicable at a cutoff when (a) it was published at or before the cutoff, (b) it is the newest schedule vintage published by the cutoff, (c) it covers the forward window the rule needs, and (d) it names every required release type. Condition (b) replaces the 24h decay window: a calendar is superseded, not stale.
candidates.rationale: A 24-hour window measures when a document was last observed, which for a schedule published months ahead is months. The risk it prices is different: using a revision that did not exist at the cutoff, or a release date that moved after the cutoff. Conditions (a), (b) and (d) price that risk directly, and for the case that matters they are stricter than an age window.
candidates.subsequent_changes: A release rescheduled after the cutoff keeps its pre-cutoff date inside the record, because that is the date the model could have known. The movement is stored as a separate amendment with its own publication time and can never rewrite an earlier morning. If a release inside the window is added after the cutoff, the morning keeps the record it was built from and the addition is reported as a data revision, not silently absorbed.

effect.reason: no imported calendar bundle exists, so the supplied freshness rule and the applicability rule both block every morning; the size of the proposal cannot be measured until a schedule is imported

evidence: The supplied contract asks for event windows and a known-release list, both derived from a schedule rather than from an observation.
BLS, BEA and FOMC publish their schedules in advance and revise them; the revision is the event to price, not the reading.
No calendar bundle has been imported yet, so the proposal is published without a measured count instead of with an estimated one.
candidates.disproof: Find one session where the schedule in force at the cutoff differs from the newest schedule published by the cutoff for a release inside the window, or where a post-cutoff revision changes a date the model would have used. Either finding voids the candidate for that session.
candidates.does_not_license: It does not license a schedule without a publication timestamp, a scraped calendar of unknown vintage, or dropping the required release-type check. It also does not license reading a release outcome early.

candidates.title: Decide the Bundesbank same-day publication bound on evidence, not on convenience
candidates.supplied_rule: published_at_utc = T+1 at 23:59 Europe/Berlin, a bound that cannot be earlier than the real publication; freshness window 96h
candidates.supplied_outcome: 697 of 725 mornings fresh; 28 blocked, worst age 151h against a 96h window
candidates.proposed_rule: Keep the strict bound as the default. A same-day bound may be adopted only if the Bundesbank's own BBSIS update stamp is captured for the dates in question, showing the T value available before the next 05:00 London cutoff.
candidates.rationale: The strict bound is the only one that cannot be a lookahead. Its cost is now visible: every operand is only available from 23:59 Berlin on the day after its date, so the newest common observation at a cutoff is at least one day older than the date it carries, and a holiday on either side adds days. On 28 mornings that pushes the age past the 96h window, to a worst case of 151h.
evidence: Two observed BBSIS refreshes, both same-day: `last update,2026-11-19 12:22:17` (the file already carried the 2026-11-19 value) and `last update,2026-11-20 12:29:01` (the file already carried the 2026-11-20 value), both read on 2026-11-20. Neither is a historical 2024 stamp.

The strict bound (23:59 Europe/Berlin on T+1) sits 35.5 hours after the later observed refresh, so it cannot be earlier than a refresh that keeps the same daily pattern; that the 2024 pattern was the same is supported by two stamps a year apart and is not proven by them.
candidates.disproof: Capture one historical BBSIS update stamp for a 2024 date that is later than the following 05:00 London cutoff. That voids the same-day claim for that date and keeps the strict bound.
candidates.does_not_license: It does not license dropping the publication clock, using a US close as a Berlin publication time, or filling a missing common date. The spread is still built on common observation dates only.

next_data_action.title: H1 is blocked on the gold fixing and the event schedule; three rule decisions are open
next_data_action.detail: Seven of the nine inputs carry imported evidence: `vix`, `front`, `spread`, `real`, `broad` and `qqq` were acquired from the agencies that publish them, and `ice` was supplied by H1-A01 as a labelled DXY.cash tape whose first completed 05:00 bar is 2024-12-12, so 455 of 725 mornings have a proxy value. `gold` and `calendar` have no evidence at all: the LBMA price host answers 403 to every request from this environment and the publisher states that historical benchmark data requires an IBA licence, so `gold` is a paid-access decision; no release schedule has been archived with a publication timestamp. Three supplied rules also block mornings on their own terms, and each is published as a measured candidate rather than applied: H1-C01, whose observation-age window leaves 161 of 725 broad mornings behind while the publication clock is never more than 175.75 hours behind the cutoff; H1-C02, whose 24-hour window cannot be met by a schedule published months ahead; and H1-C03, whose strict Bundesbank next-day bound costs 28 spread mornings. A receipt is required only for sealed live replay, and no receipt exists yet.
steps: Buy an IBA licence for the LBMA Gold Price PM USD history (the publisher states a licence is required for historical benchmark data), then import `gold` with the supplied five-fixing transform; do not substitute OANDA XAU/USD.
Archive the BLS, BEA and FOMC schedules with their publication timestamps, then import `calendar` as a vintage-stamped record; do not scrape a calendar of unknown vintage.
Decide H1-C01: measure H.10 freshness on the publication clock with the latest-release condition, instead of on the observation date.
Decide H1-C02: treat a schedule as applicable knowledge (published by the cutoff, newest vintage, complete release types) instead of as a decaying observation.
Decide H1-C03: keep the strict Bundesbank next-day bound, or capture BBSIS update stamps that support a same-day bound for the dates in question.

notes: This is the agreed test 1. The broker series is a proxy for the official index and is labelled as a proxy everywhere it appears.
A flat window inside the flat band is excluded from the accuracy denominator and counted separately.

h1_readiness.status: blocked on the H1.1 evidence contract

definitions.label: USD-only opposite-direction mapping in four markets
definitions.question: Did the same USD call point the right way in EUR/USD, gold, bitcoin and the NAS100 over the same window?
definitions.status_label: scored market by market; no cross-market aggregate is published or reported
notes: This is the agreed test 2: one model call against four market outcomes, not a pair-combination measure.
Each market carries its own denominator; an aggregate across markets is not reported.

h1_readiness.status: blocked on the H1.1 evidence contract

definitions.label: Original Layer 2 levels with the frozen 5R rules
definitions.question: When a Layer 1 call was handed to the original Layer 2 levels, did the frozen 5R path reach its target before its stop?
definitions.status_label: blocked on history: the simulation is implemented and unit-tested, but no 5-minute tape or level ladder exists
definitions.outcome_source: one-hour closes with the original layer-2 level grid and 5R management
notes: This is the agreed test 3. It needs a trade-qualified call, contemporaneous levels and an actionable bid/ask M5 replay.
The path rule engine is implemented and unit-tested on synthetic tapes (lib/layer1_backtesting/l2l_simulation.js). That is a statement about the simulator, not a measured result.
The grid does not yet exist for these markets, so the test is blocked on history, not scored at zero.

accounting.statement: Costs, 1% sizing, equity and drawdown are implemented from contracts.ACCOUNT and demonstrated on a labelled fixture. No historical trade path exists to apply them to.

simulation.statement: The frozen 5R path rule is implemented and unit-tested on synthetic tapes. The historical 5-minute tape and level ladder are absent, so the rule has never been measured on history.

h1_readiness.status: blocked on the H1.1 evidence contract

definitions.label: Original levels plus midpoints with the frozen 3R rules
definitions.question: With midpoints added to the original levels, did the frozen 3R path reach its target before its stop?
definitions.status_label: blocked on history: the simulation is implemented and unit-tested, but no 5-minute tape or level ladder exists
definitions.outcome_source: one-hour closes with the levels-plus-midpoints grid and 3R management
notes: This is the agreed test 4, a separately frozen geometry and management rule, not a sensitivity check on test 3.
It needs the same tape and ladder evidence as test 3 plus the midpoint geometry.
The midpoint ladder and the 3R path are implemented and unit-tested on synthetic tapes; the historical inputs are absent.

accounting.statement: Costs, 1% sizing, equity and drawdown are implemented from contracts.ACCOUNT and demonstrated on a labelled fixture. No historical trade path exists to apply them to.

simulation.statement: The levels-plus-midpoints ladder and the frozen 3R path are implemented and unit-tested on synthetic tapes. The historical 5-minute tape and level ladder are absent, so the rule has never been measured on history.

hypotheses.text: Each family carries one unit of weight and each usable signal inside it votes equally; the adjudications validate no weight at all.
Each family votes as the arithmetic mean of its usable signals, capped to [-1, +1]; a family with fewer usable signals still votes for those it has.
A direction exists only outside the frozen 0.20 deadband; inside it, or on an exact net zero, the morning is NO_CALL.
The trade floor is band 3 with all twelve signals usable and a readable event family. It is a study floor, not an edge.
A missing input makes its signal unusable; nothing is carried forward, proxied or filled from a later print.
The US-DE 2Y spread input is absent on an unstated number of 725 mornings, so the F3 spread rule cannot vote on those mornings even though the row is mapped.
Every one of the 25 adjudications is disposition Blocked: no sign, weight or threshold is validated by the adjudication that produced it.
The dollar series behind F5 is a broad trade-weighted index stand-in, not the official ICE cash DXY.
The control treats a neutral Fed bias as a missing input, so a neutral statement removes F8 from the vote instead of voting neutral.
The book carries no timeframe field: all 25 rows are applied to the 05:00 London session, so no row is specifically an H1 rule.

mapping_review.verdict: The mapping is incomplete: at least one adjudication has no enforced executable rule.

decisions.question: Does pair-combination accuracy mean two independent Layer 1 legs, or the existing USD-only cross-market test?
decisions.decision: Keep the agreed USD-only inverse cross-market test. It is one USD call against four market outcomes and it is test 3. Combining two independent Layer 1 calls is a separate future test with its own definition.
decisions.previous_recommendation: Define it as two independent legs and leave it unscored until a non-USD leg has a frozen rulebook; the four-market test already answers a different question.
effect: tests.four_markets keeps its name, its four per-market denominators and its USD-only reading.
pair_combination is registered as a future test and remains unscored; it is not renamed onto test 3.
decisions.does_not_license: It does not license a second leg, a long/short leg mapping or a pair-level accuracy number.

decisions.question: Which gate defines published readiness and accuracy: presence and freshness, or present + fresh + clocked + identified?
decisions.decision: Headline readiness uses the selected model's strict evidence gate. Each performance result uses its own eligible sample and displays its denominator beside it.
decisions.previous_recommendation: Publish both, labelled; the narrow gate keeps today's numbers comparable and the strict gate keeps the research honest.
effect: Headline ready mornings for either model are the strict-gate count, which is 0 of 725 because no 05:00 receipt exists.
The narrow-gate count stays visible as a labelled comparison, never as the headline.
Every test row prints the sample that produced it; the legacy reconstructed sample is never presented as the strict-gate sample.
decisions.does_not_license: It does not license a single blended accuracy figure, and it does not upgrade a proxy test to a headline.

decisions.question: Should the trade flags on blocked mornings be withdrawn, relabelled, or kept?
decisions.decision: A blocked morning creates no valid decision and no trade. Any contradictory legacy trade flag is preserved as an audit finding, not deleted and not traded.
decisions.previous_recommendation: Yes, or relabel them as conditional; the engine already refuses to publish them and the difference is counted under reconciliation.
effect: The engine keeps trade_eligible false on every blocked or abstained morning.
The published flag is retained and counted under engine_stricter and in the run audit as trade_on_blocked_morning.
The screen shows those flags as audit findings with their dates, never as eligible trades.
decisions.does_not_license: It does not license rewriting the published artefact, and it does not turn a withdrawn flag into a trade.

decisions.question: Is the flat band and the scoring tie policy frozen for the USD session?
decisions.decision: The exact proposed flat bands and the tie treatment are returned per instrument below. They are frozen from development dates only, before any holdout outcome is examined.
decisions.previous_recommendation: Freeze both before any candidate is scored, as the handover requires.
effect: Each instrument carries one band, its development sample and its rule; the band is applied unchanged to the 400 unseen mornings.
A move strictly inside the band is flat: excluded from the accuracy denominator and counted separately.
A vote that nets exactly zero, or sits inside the 0.20 deadband, is NO_CALL; there is no coin flip and no direction-priority tie-break.
decisions.does_not_license: It does not license re-fitting a band after seeing a holdout result, and it does not license dropping flat mornings silently.

decisions.question: Which coverage figure is authoritative for the candidate: the coverage table's reconstructed calls or the engine's gated calls?
decisions.decision: Trace both to their model, gate, dates and source artefact, show their overlap and exclusions, and report scheduled, reconstructed, valid, directional and scored counts separately. Neither figure is authoritative for the other.
decisions.previous_recommendation: State the coverage rule beside every accuracy figure and treat the table as a reconstruction, not as the model's published call count.
effect: The report and the screen print five counts per model with their own definitions and denominators.
The scored denominator of the broker-proxy test is labelled as the legacy reconstructed sample, because it contains calls the gated engine would not make.
No claim is made that one count is a subset of another; the overlap and the exclusions are printed.
decisions.does_not_license: It does not license treating 515 reconstructed calls as 515 valid calls, or treating 121 gate-passing calls as a scored sample of that size.

legend.blocked: a data gap: a required input, an instrument or a receipt was not in hand at 05:00
legend.valid_abstention: the book had the evidence and chose not to call: every blocking check passed and no trade is implied
legend.no_call: the book was eligible but the vote sat inside the deadband or netted exactly zero
legend.allowed: the implemented book produced a direction; it is not a valid call for the intended H1 package
legend.scored: the morning's outcome is stored and entered a denominator
legend.scored_in_legacy_aggregate: scored in the published aggregate on a reconstructed call, not in the gated sample
legend.not_in_legacy_sample: the engine allows the morning but the published reconstructed call set does not contain it
legend.unmapped: no decision record exists for the morning
